jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Infotainment HMI Systems
jobs.description:
About Us

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Role Summary

The Berlin team is looking for a Staff Software Engineer - Infotainment, to provide hands-on technical leadership for complex embedded software and hardware/software integration work. You will help shape architectures that connect vehicle hardware, embedded operating systems, platform services, communication paths, and user-facing behavior into reliable products.

This is a broad technical role for an engineer who can move comfortably between system-level design and implementation. You will work across current and next-generation vehicle platforms, helping teams take ideas from early architecture through development, integration, validation, and production readiness. You’ll be working in a high-performing forward-deployed team working closely with key OEM stakeholders. Examples include physical input, HMI systems and bespoke in-vehicle touchpoints.

This role is based in our Berlin office and requires a minimum of three days per week onsite.

Responsibilities

  • Architect, design, develop, and maintain embedded software across hardware interfaces, operating-system services, middleware, communication paths, and applications, using C/C++ and contributing to Rust adoption where it improves safety, reliability, maintainability, or service boundaries.

  • Lead technical design discussions and translate ambiguous requirements into clear interfaces, ownership boundaries, acceptance criteria, dependencies, delivery plans, reusable abstractions, and configuration contracts that scale across vehicle platforms, products, and variants.

  • Evaluate and optimize constrained systems for CPU, memory, storage, power, latency, startup, concurrency, and fault handling while ensuring predictable behavior, reliability, and maintainability.

  • Guide the integration of hardware-linked behavior—including physical controls, display interaction, vehicle signals, persistent state, device configuration, and other time-sensitive system behavior—across software and hardware components.

  • Lead complex software and hardware investigations and drive end-to-end validation using logs, traces, diagnostics, target hardware, laboratory equipment, simulators, emulators, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and prototype vehicles.

  • Partner with hardware, firmware, platform, application, validation, product, and external teams to resolve dependencies and make timely technical decisions; establish practices for schemas, generated bindings, diagnostics, observability, versioning, compatibility, and maintainability; and mentor engineers while communicating architecture, risks, trade-offs, and decisions clearly.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus seven or more years developing or integrating embedded, platform, or hardware-linked software.

  • Strong hands-on experience developing, debugging, reviewing, and maintaining C and/or C++ software, with practical Rust experience or the ability and interest to learn Rust.

  • Experience with embedded operating systems, embedded Linux, real-time systems, board-support packages, device drivers, hypervisor-based systems, or comparable constrained computing environments.

  • Strong understanding of hardware/software interfaces, communication protocols, concurrency, timing, startup and reset behavior, resource constraints, fault handling, and system performance across CPU, power, memory, storage, latency, reliability, and degraded operation.

  • Experience leading architecture, integration, and system-level debugging across multiple software and hardware components, defining interface contracts, schemas, generated bindings, diagnostics, logging, versioning, compatibility practices, and end-to-end validation.

  • Experience with automotive, aerospace, mobile-device, consumer-electronics, robotics, industrial-control, defense, or similarly constrained embedded products, including HMI, physical controls, display systems, vehicle signals, gateways, input routing, or other real-time hardware-linked behavior.

  • Experience with ARM-based systems, high-performance system-on-chip platforms, board bring-up, hardware debugging tools, and interfaces such as CAN, Ethernet, USB, PCIe, SPI, or I2C; familiarity with reusable platform, middleware, SDK, or device-integration components, CI/CD, telemetry, diagnostic logging, command-line tooling, and laboratory-debugging workflows, plus excellent communication skills across distributed teams and external partners.

Total Rewards

We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program.

Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. This role is also eligible for equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), subject to board approval and the terms of our equity incentive plans, including applicable vesting requirements.

In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. Offerings vary by country. Learn more about our global benefit programs.

External candidates can apply for this role through the Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies careers site (https://rivianvw.tech/#careers). If you are a current employee, please apply through our internal job board.

Equal Opportunity

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law. We are also committed to ensuring compliance with all applicable fair employment practice laws regarding citizenship and immigration status.

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at ----- style="min-height:1.5em">

Candidate Data Privacy

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies” may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) record keeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies affiliates; and (iii) Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies’ service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies may transfer or store internationally your Candidate Personal Data, including to or in the United States, Canada, and the European Union and in the cloud, and this data may be subject to the laws and accessible to the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of such jurisdictions.

If you provide a mobile telephone number as part of your application or during the recruitment process, Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies may use that number to contact you via SMS text message for recruitment-related purposes, including scheduling, logistics, and status updates. jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Vehicle Configuration Platform
jobs.description:
About Us

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Role Summary

A single firmware release must serve every vehicle variant we build across both Rivian and all Volkswagen brands. The vehicle configuration platform that the OTA team supports makes that possible: a schema-driven system that defines every configurable attribute of a vehicle and provisions them onto vehicles in the factory, in service, and over the air customer updates. Getting this wrong can mean anything from the wrong information showing on the driver display to a car that needs to be towed in for service.

You will be a technical leader on the team that owns this platform, working as a peer to its lead architect. Where the architect drives the structural evolution of the configuration system itself, you will own the health, reliability, and scalability of everything around it: the compilation and code generation pipelines, the validation and release infrastructure, the provisioning path from schema to vehicle, and the developer experience of every engineer who touches configuration. You will set technical direction for this surface area, drive initiatives that span firmware, build infrastructure, release engineering, OTA, and factory integration across two companies' engineering organizations, and raise the bar for how the team designs, reviews, and ships.

This role is based in our Berlin office and requires a minimum of three days per week onsite, with occasional travel to other company and partner sites as needed.

 

Responsibilities

  • Own the technical direction for configuration tooling, validation, and delivery infrastructure, translating platform architecture into a concrete, sequenced roadmap and driving it to completion across teams.

  • Lead initiatives that simplify the platform: consolidating redundant mechanisms, retiring legacy pathways, and reducing the coordination cost of routine changes, while every downstream consumer keeps working.

  • Design the compatibility strategy for data contracts deployed to devices in the field, and build the automated enforcement that makes schema evolution provably safe rather than carefully reviewed.

  • Architect the validation and release pipeline as a product: define what classes of defects must be impossible to merge, and build the layered checks, staged rollouts, and observability that get there.

jobs.description:
Your creative field

We are looking for a full-time, permanent Senior Network Engineer to start as soon as possible. We live remote-first, but you have the freedom to choose whether you want to work hybrid or completely on-site due to your proximity to one of our locations (Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg, Munich).


Contabo Group operates one of Europe's largest cloud infrastructure platforms, with data centres across Europe and beyond. As our new Senior Network Engineer, you take on the network backbone that thousands of customers rely on every day, with real ownership from day one.

Right now, the biggest milestone on your plate is the build out of our new AI data centre. You inherit a fully designed Leaf-Spine architecture built on Arista EOS, BGP EVPN, and VXLAN, take ownership of it, refine it where it needs refining, and drive everything from commissioning through to stable production operations. Alongside that, you keep our existing LTG infrastructure running reliably: you design, build, and operate complex network, server, and security systems, analyse and resolve faults, and harden our network security through scrubbers, firewalls, ACLs, and NAC.

You monitor network traffic and infrastructure performance, extrapolate the KPIs that matter to management, and coordinate with external service providers and remote hands across the globe. You keep our network diagrams, runbooks, change logs, and system documentation in good shape, and you work closely with Platform Engineering on Cilium BGP peering, Kubernetes node network configuration, and IPAM, acting as the ongoing interface between NetOps and Platform.

You join a self-organising, agile team that owns its problems end to end, from analysis to resolution, without micromanagement. On top of that, you will have real room to grow into infrastructure automation, DDoS mitigation with Nokia Deepfield, observability, and BGP EVPN fabric engineering, alongside plenty of national and international project work.

You report directly to our Head of Network and become the permanent owner of everything networking related at Contabo Group, Blue and Black alike. Communication, team orientation, problem solving, and analytical thinking matter just as much here as deep technical expertise, since you will regularly work across teams and explain complex topics to people outside networking.


What convinces us

Your personality, paired with: 

  • minimum 5 years of hands-on experience with complex, scalable networks and fabric infrastructures on Cisco and/or Arista, ideally with real Leaf-Spine and BGP EVPN VXLAN exposure
  • strong expertise in WAN connectivity, data centre peering, uplink management, VPN, and IPv6
  • strong expertise in security administration and DDoS mitigation (e.g. Nokia Deepfield, Aurologic), plus solid monitoring skills with tools like Grafana, Check_MK, or Zabbix

  • strong analytical and strategic thinking, paired with clear, confident communication
  • a results-driven, hands-on mindset with a high standard of performance, customer orientation, and composure under pressure
  • genuine team spirit, reliability, and a self-driven way of working that thrives without micromanagement

  • strong conflict-handling skills, a knack for building contacts across teams, and openness to change
  • a basic understanding of Kubernetes networking, ideally paired with an Arista certification (or equivalent Cisco knowledge), a completed IT apprenticeship or equivalent, and German language skills alongside excellent English
We know that you may not currently meet all the requirements. But if you come to us with the right amount of commitment and enthusiasm, we can take off together and make a big difference.

jobs.title: Marketing Data Scientist
jobs.description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We're looking for a Data Scientist to support ElevenLabs' offline media and strategic marketing bets: from OOH billboards to niche sponsorships and experimental brand campaigns. You'll build the frameworks that tell us whether a channel with no click to track is actually working, partnering closely with Marketing and the Growth Data team.

  • Design and run measurement for offline / out-of-home campaigns: geo holdout tests, matched-market tests, media mix modelling and incrementality studies.

  • Partner directly with Marketing leadership on which niche channels, markets or formats to test next, and size the bet.

  • Build models that combine offline spend data with digital and product signals into one coherent view of marketing effectiveness.

  • Work alongside the Growth Data team's digital marketing data scientists to keep offline and online measurement consistent.

Requirements

Demonstrated experience measuring marketing effectiveness, ideally including offline, brand or hard-to-track channels (OOH, TV, podcast, sponsorship, events).

  • Strong SQL and Python, with experience in causal inference, media mix modelling or incrementality testing.

  • Comfort designing measurement without a clean click-level signal, and communicating uncertainty honestly.

  • Strong stakeholder management with Marketing / Brand leadership, able to turn a strategic question into a testable plan.

  • Structured thinker comfortable with ambiguity: this is a newer, less-defined function.

Bonus:

  • Experience specifically with OOH, billboard or experiential campaign measurement.

  • Experience with media mix modelling tools or frameworks (Robyn, Recast, LightweightMMM or similar).

  • Experience partnering with brand or creative teams on niche or unconventional marketing bets.

Location

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Europe or the US East Coast, with the ability to operate in CET / ET timezones required. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, Warsaw, Dublin or New York.

  • Die Disziplin führen und weiterentwickeln: Übernimm die disziplinarische Führung für drei KI-Engineers und hilf ihnen dabei, sich zu Engineers zu entwickeln, die den technischen Maßstab selbst setzen.

  • Hands-on bleiben: Rund 70 Prozent deiner Zeit verbringst du im Code, an den Problemen, bei denen dein Urteilsvermögen am meisten zählt. Der Rest entfällt auf technische und disziplinarische Führung.

Was du mitbringst

Wir suchen einen Engineer mit einem soliden Software-Engineering-Fundament und echter Praxiserfahrung mit agentenbasierten Systemen in Produktion, der eine Disziplin führen möchte, statt nur an einer Codebase zu arbeiten. Damit unsere Stellenanzeigen leichter lesbar sind, verwenden wird im Textverlauf die männliche Form der Anrede. Bei Flip sind alle willkommen ganz egal, welches Geschlecht du hast oder wie alt du bist. Sexuelle Identität, Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung und Behinderungen spielen keine Rolle. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Platform & Infrastructure (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
The product you will work on

The HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. HOLOPLOT deployed Matrix Arrays in various venues, including the Sphere in Las Vegas - the world’s most advanced entertainment venue and, notably, home to the world’s largest audio installation in entertainment. 


Audio processing in HOLOPLOT systems is distributed: every loudspeaker runs embedded Linux, and hundreds of them have to be configured, coordinated, monitored, and updated as one system. This is enabled by multiple open source and in-house developed services running on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. AWS-hosted services connect venues to remote monitoring, telemetry, and configuration. Many venues are air-gapped or only intermittently connected for remote servicing, and that constraint shapes most of the design decisions in the platform.


The ideal candidate is

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who builds the platform our sound systems run on, and who takes responsibility for how it behaves in production.


This is a software engineering role first. You will spend your time writing software, either with your own team or embedded with one of the other HOLOPLOT teams: services, controllers, agents, and tooling that provision, configure, observe, and update our systems. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. You design the operational side, you build it, and you are on call when it misbehaves in the field.


Your role and responsibilities

You will join the team that owns the platform underneath our installations and connected services, working alongside backend, embedded, and frontend engineers who are organized in cross-functional product teams.


Build the platform

  • Architect and implement services to provision, configure, and manage server fleets across AWS and local clusters.

  • Create control-plane logic for venue systems to ensure consistency, health monitoring, rollout management, and recovery, even during uplink disruptions.

  • Establish end-to-end provisioning workflows for embedded Linux hardware, spanning from initial manufacturing to customer deployment.

  • Enhance update processes to streamline software deployments for active customer installations.

  • Develop APIs and developer tooling that empower engineering teams to independently deploy, observe, and troubleshoot their services.

  • Embed telemetry capabilities into the platform to facilitate remote diagnosis of venue system behavior

  • .

Run what you build

  • Own the AWS infrastructure behind our connected services: remote access, access control, telemetry ingestion, remote backup, secret management, and monitoring. All of it is infrastructure as code.

  • Operate and evolve the on-premises Kubernetes footprint at venues, including air-gapped and intermittently connected installations.

  • Monitor large environments, investigate problems across the software/hardware boundary, and turn each incident into a fix in the code.

  • Be part of a compensated on-call rotation


Set the technical direction

  • Advise and collaborate with product teams on building distributed systems that are scalable, secure, and observable, and review their designs with production reality in mind.

  • Research and introduce tools and technologies where they measurably improve how we build and operate.

  • Contribute back to the open-source projects we depend on, through issues and fixes.


What you need to succeed in this role

  • Several years of professional software engineering experience, most of it spent designing and shipping production systems.

  • Fluency in software engineering as a craft: concurrency, error handling, testing, and designing APIs that other teams build on.

  • Working knowledge of the Kubernetes control plane and the operator/controller pattern, including how clusters behave when they are unhealthy.

  • Hands-on experience with AWS, and a firm belief in infrastructure as code. Terraform and Ansible are what we use today.

  • Comfort across several languages, and the ability to pick up a new one when the problem calls for it. Our platform work is mostly Go and Python, with Rust and C++ elsewhere in the stack.

  • Experience building distributed systems, and a clear understanding of how they fail: partitions, partial rollouts, clock skew, retries, and reconciliation.

  • A good sense for software architecture and maintainability, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can pick up and change.

  • A strong command of Linux, scripting, and automation.

  • Experience instrumenting software for telemetry and using it to answer real questions about running systems.

  • Good judgment about what to automate and what to leave alone.

  • Strong communication skills in English. You can explain a design or a failure clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and non-specialists.

  • Willingness to take part in compensated on-call and weekend work when installations need it.

  • A can-do mentality, an eye for detail, and the courage to take on problems outside your comfort zone.

  • Experience in using AI for engineering.


Nice to haves

  • Experience with NATS, Prometheus/Thanos, or PostgreSQL in production.

  • Experience with air-gapped or intermittently connected installations.

  • Experience running Kubernetes in production, not only deploying to it.

  • Experience with embedded Linux, device fleet management, or IoT security.

  • Networking depth: multicast at scale, WireGuard, BGP, IPv6.

  • Experience in the audio, broadcast, or live events industry.

  • Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects


We offer you

At HOLOPLOT we work in a flexible hybrid setup with trust-based working hours, giving you the freedom to organise your day in a way that supports focus, deep work and balance. Pay is competitive and fair, and we offer perks and benefits such as subsidised public transport, lunch allowances, Urban Sports and a company pension scheme.

You’ll join an international, open-minded team across software, hardware, product and research, in an environment with plenty of autonomy and ownership. You’ll work on cutting-edge audio technology, turn complex requirements into working solutions and contribute to global projects, with support for your growth through individual development plans, mentoring and coaching.

jobs.title: Data Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us 

IVC Evidensia is the UK and Europe’s leading veterinary care group, made up of over 900 practices and referral hospitals, united by a shared purpose of happier animals, happier owners. 

At IVC Evidensia, we believe careers should be built without limits. Our people are supported to make more impact, access more career opportunities, and play an active role in their local and professional communities. Through investment in learning, innovation, and wellbeing, we create environments where our teams can grow in confidence, capability, and fulfilment—at every stage of their career. 

As part of Central Functions, you will be part of the teams that support and enable our network of over 2,500 practices across 20 countries, driving operational excellence, innovation, and strategic impact across the business.  

Our Technology teams are responsible for the systems and infrastructure that make that work - everything our healthcare professionals need to deliver world-class care. From keeping on top of patient records, health plans, client communications, diary management and dispensing, our teams have a lot to think about and need smarter ways to provide the convenience and expertise that modern Pet owners have come to expect.

IVC Evidensia is undergoing an exciting digital transformation. The key to this is improving the management of our core data sets - accelerating the standardisation of operational systems in practices, building stronger master data management tooling, and developing standard reporting models across the group.

As a data engineer, you will work with the team to advance the data platform within a DevOps culture. You will play a central role in building and maintaining scalable data pipelines across Databricks & Azure SQL Server, and will bring solid experience with ELT, orchestration, and scripting languages. A firm grasp of data modelling and management will be essential throughout.

The role

The Data Engineer will be a technical authority accountable for the design and development of the technologies that underpin our data strategy. At the heart of this is our Databricks data platform, and you will take ownership of building, optimising, and maintaining data pipelines using PySpark - orchestrating feeds from source systems through to our group data platform and taking technical ownership of all parts of the process.

You will work closely with the business to deliver solutions that address real challenges, engaging with SMEs to break requirements into deliverables. You will also collaborate with the Data Architect to shape our overarching data management strategy.

What you'll bring to the role

We're looking for a technically skilled and business aware individual with a strong understanding of data concepts, including storage, processing, and modelling. Core requirements include:

  • Databricks - hands-on experience building and managing workloads on the Databricks platform, including Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, and Declarative Automation Bundles
  • PySpark - proficiency in writing and optimising PySpark code for data transformation and processing
  • Azure - solid experience working within the Azure ecosystem, including services such as Azure Data Factory, Azure Data Lake Storage, and Azure DevOps
  • Azure SQL Server - experience with Azure SQL Server is important, as it forms the foundation of our existing data warehouse. You will be working across both our SQL Server environment and our Databricks platform, and an understanding of how the two integrate will be key to success in this role
  • ELT & pipeline development - experience designing and maintaining pipelines using REST APIs, JSON, and ELT protocols
  • Data modelling - comfort working with both relational and non-relational data technologies, with a solid grounding in modelling principles

Exposure to business intelligence tools like Power BI is desirable. You'll act as a key interface between IT and functions such as Finance and Marketing, so excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills are vital.

You should be confident working within an Agile framework, with an understanding of secure development practices and non-functional requirements such as scalability, performance, and access management. An international mindset, sensitivity to local business priorities, and a collaborative approach are essential.

What’s in it for you? 
At IVC Evidensia, we’re committed to supporting your development and wellbeing.

When you join us, you’ll benefit from: 
A role with real business impact supporting teams across the organisation 
Clear career pathways with progression opportunities within Central Functions and beyond 
Ongoing learning and development supported by tailored programmes and resources 
A collaborative, values-led culture focused on care, innovation, and continuous improvement 
Flexible working with a remote first working policy

Discounted staff pet care  
Access to discounts/cashback with hundreds of participating retailers

jobs.title: Planning and Supply Chain Manager
jobs.description:
Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include the most energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges.

Join Us at the Forefront of Quantum Computing Innovation 🚀 

At Quandela, we're moving from an R&D-driven organization toward a structured, scalable industrial operation. We're looking for a builder as much as a manager to create our end-to-end supply chain, from demand to customer delivery. Your first major challenge: build our S&OP process from the ground up. You'll move easily between strategy and execution, from running an S&OP review and an 18-month capacity outlook to solving a critical component shortage or securing an urgent customer shipment. 

Your Key Responsibilities

  • Build the S&OP process from scratch: define governance, meeting cadence, roles, inputs and KPIs, then progressively mature it as the company scales 
  • Lead monthly cross-functional S&OP reviews with Sales, Operations, Production, R&D, Purchasing, Finance and Management, and establish a single shared view of demand, supply and customer commitments
  • Consolidate demand from customer orders, weighted commercial forecasts, internal R&D needs, qualification activities and strategic programs into a rolling forecast
  • Build and maintain the Master Production Schedule, with planning horizons adapted to our long manufacturing and supply lead times
  • Translate demand into capacity, resource, material and supplier requirements, identify gaps and develop scenarios to support management decisions on priorities and commitments
  • Turn the production plan into executable schedules, monitor WIP and progress, and coordinate recovery plans when delays or shortages occur
  • Structure purchasing and MRP processes, define sourcing strategies based on lead time, criticality, supply risk, cost and MOQ, and track supplier performance (OTD, quality, responsiveness)
  • Define inventory principles and safety-stock strategies for critical components, while managing excess, obsolete and slow-moving stock
  • Organize inbound, internal and outbound logistics, including the transport of fragile, sensitive and high-value technological products
  • Manage customs and international trade: import/export documentation, classification, country of origin, Incoterms and compliance, in coordination with forwarders and brokers
  • Contribute to the selection and deployment of ERP/MRP and planning tools, reduce reliance on manual spreadsheets and build clear supply chain dashboards
  • Define and track key KPIs (forecast accuracy, plan adherence, supplier and customer OTD/OTIF, inventory turns, shortages, lead times) and drive continuous improvement

Requirements

  • Master's degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Engineering or a related field 
  • 5+ years of experience in planning, supply chain or industrial operations
  • Proven experience implementing or running an S&OP process 
  • APICS / ASCM certification (CPIM, CSCP)
  • Strong command of demand and production planning, scheduling, MRP, purchasing, inventory management and logistics 
  • Hands-on experience with ERP/MRP systems
  • Strong analytical skills and ability to turn complex data into clear priorities and decisions
  • Excellent communication and cross-functional coordination skills
  • Thrives in a fast-changing, growing organization
  • Fluent French and English 

 Nice to have 

  • Experience in semiconductor, photonics, electronics or other high-tech manufacturing
  • Foundries, outsourced manufacturing and long-lead-time, critical-component supply chains
  • International suppliers and customers, customs and international logistics
  • ERP implementation or supply chain digitalization; advanced Excel or Power BI 

Benefits

  • Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience
  • Profit-sharing & company savings plan
  • 100% health coverage (Alan)
  • 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
  • Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
  • Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)

What we offer:

  • A meaningful role with real ownership, from day one
  • A team eager to collaborate and grow with you
  • A hybrid work model (3 days/week onsite in Massy, 1 day in Paris, 1 to 2 days remotely)
  • Daily exposure to the entire quantum stack — from high-level APIs to low-level firmware, and everything in between.

jobs.title: Mobile frontend engineering
jobs.description:
Making preventive health the default for every human in Europe

 

The mission

At Lucis, we believe healthcare should be preventive, not reactive. We’re building the OS for human longevity to help people add more healthy years to their lives. You can read more about who we are and how we work here.

 

The role

We’ve processed 200,000+ clinical tests across 4 countries with a team of 20. We’re growing 10% week over week. And we’re still early.

We’re looking for a mobile frontend engineer who treats the app as a craft, not a checklist. You care about the half-pixel, the spring curve on a transition, the way a screen feels in the hand, and you can build it. You own the mobile experience end-to-end in our monorepo, orchestrate AI to execute, and raise the bar for everyone around you.

You won’t spend your days writing boilerplate. You’ll write specs that agents execute, review AI-generated code with a critical eye, and make decisions that compound over time. This is what engineering looks like now. If that excites you, keep reading.

What we’re looking for: Mobile frontend, design engineering & world-class craft

A confirmed mobile engineer (8+ years) with exceptional craft and a real sensibility for design. You live in Expo and React Native, you care deeply about how the product feels, and you don’t wait for designs to be ready to propose something delightful. You have also experience building native experience. You think in interactions, motion, and detail.

You’ll own what members touch every day: onboarding, the core app surfaces, the moments that turn a first-time visitor into someone who trusts us with their health. Your work has to be delightful and reliable on real devices, for people who decide in minutes whether to trust us.

 
 

About you

You’re passionate about the future of human health and want your work to help people stay healthy for longer. You move quickly from idea to execution, take full ownership of what you build, and work best with talented people who care as much as you do.

 

You thrive in fast‑moving environments, learn by doing, and value feedback as a way to continuously improve. You use AI the way others use a calculator: naturally, to go faster and think bigger.

 

You’ll fit in well if

  • You've shipped at least one product from 0→1 and felt the difference between writing code and building a system

  • You have 2 deep areas of expertise and can operate across the full stack when the situation demands it

  • You write specs before you write code — precise enough that an AI agent executes correctly on the first pass

  • You review AI-generated code with the same rigor you'd apply to a junior engineer's PR: edge cases, security gaps, design smell

  • You bias toward shipping. A good decision today beats a perfect one next week

  • You're genuinely interested in health — maybe you track your own biomarkers, or you're just frustrated that healthcare is still reactive

 

We would not be a fit if

  • You need a clearly scoped role before you can operate

  • You measure output in lines of code written

  • You've only worked in large orgs with dedicated infra, QA, and platform teams

  • You optimize for stability over velocity

 

Our current stack

TypeScript monorepo · React Native · NestJS · PostgreSQL + Prisma · AWS (Terraform, Qovery) · GitHub Actions · Claude Code + Cursor

 

The process

  • Intro call (20 min): culture & role fit.

  • Technical interview (30 min)

  • At-home case study: hands-on project, delivery in 2 days.

  • Deep dive (90 min) and team chat (on-site)

  • Reference calls

 

How we work

We work together from our Paris hub. We’re passionate about what we’re building and believe the fastest way to create something exceptional is side by side. We’re open to relocation support for the right individuals, and we welcome missionaries who travel to work with us in Paris on a regular basis.

 

  • Rigor without ego: Audits, science, and code all deserve the same high bar.

  • Radical ownership: Feedback loops are short; everyone contributes to building the best version of Lucis.

  • Velocity over perfection: We ship daily and prefer a good decision today over a perfect one next week.

At Lucis, AI isn't just our product, it's our engine. 100% of our teams are equipped with the best AI agents. You have carte blanche to explore and automate everything that can be, so you can focus exclusively on high-value work.

jobs.title: R&D Intern - Fairness in Deep Learning - Paris
Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy, Intern
jobs.description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

As a Software Engineer intern on Robot Autonomy, you'll work on the software that runs on our legged security robots: how they perceive their surroundings, know where they are, and move through real customer sites on patrol. You'll join the team that owns everything on the robot and take a well-scoped problem from first experiment to a result that runs on hardware.

The role focuses on building software for the robot autonomy stack that runs in the field. We'll agree your focus area with you during the interview process, based on your strengths and the team's priorities, and we expect you to own it from day one.

This role is hands-on. You'll work with real sensor data and field logs, test on physical robots, and see first-hand why a robot that works in the lab can still fail on a live site at night, in rain, or after the layout changes.

What You'll Work On

  • Build and improve components of the on-robot autonomy stack, such as perception, localisation and state estimation, or planning and navigation, depending on your background and the team's priorities.

  • Integrate sensors such as lidar, cameras and IMU, and work with the data they produce in day, night and challenging weather.

  • Reproduce issues from field deployments using logs and simulation, find the root cause, and help fix it at the right layer.

  • Design repeatable tests and clear metrics that show whether a change holds up across routes, lighting, weather and site layouts.

  • Test your work on physical robots, and join site visits to see how the system behaves in real operating conditions.

  • Apply solid engineering practices: code review, version control, reproducible experiments and clear documentation.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for a strong robotics student who wants to see their work run on real robots, not only in simulation. You don't need every item below, but you should meet the core requirements and bring depth in at least one area of the autonomy stack. You'll join a small team that moves fast, expects ownership, and holds work to the standard of running on live customer sites.

Your Background

  • Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD, or completed a Master's degree within the last year, in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field.

  • Demonstrated depth in at least one of perception, localisation and state estimation, or motion planning and navigation, through a thesis, research or a substantial project.

  • Strong coding skills in Python.

  • Hands-on experience with ROS 2.

  • Comfortable using Linux, Docker and Git in your workflows.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working with physical robots, ideally mobile or legged.

  • Experience with lidar or camera processing, SLAM, or sensor fusion.

  • Experience with robotics simulators such as Isaac Sim, Gazebo or MuJoCo.

  • Publications or competition results in robotics (ICRA, IROS, RSS, CoRL).

What We Offer

  • Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

  • Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

  • Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

  • Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

  • Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

  • Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

jobs.title: Applied AI - Member of Technical Staff
jobs.description:
About Us

We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.

Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.

The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.

Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.

Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.

In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.

We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

The Applied AI team own Callosum's customer engagements end to end. You will work directly with customer engineering teams to understand their AI workloads, design and run rigorous evaluations against their production pipelines, integrate optimised workflows into their systems, and make sure the results hold in production.

At Callosum, Applied AI Engineers are the technical bridge between what customers run and what we build. What you learn shapes the research and platform roadmap. The evaluations you run are how we prove the technology in production. As an early member of the team, you will help build the methodology, tooling, and engagement practices the function runs on. The role is engineering-led: you will employ technical judgment to recognise what kind of system a problem needs and prototype it.

You will work closely with the engineers designing new intelligent systems, with the platform team that serves them, and directly with senior technical stakeholders on the customer side. We run a flat Member of Technical Staff structure. Responsibility and scope grow with what you demonstrate, including leadership of the Applied AI function as the team scales.

What You'll Build

  • Customer engagement from first workload scoping through evaluation, integration, and production deployment

  • Design and run rigorous evaluations on customers' production workloads: set success criteria, instrument the comparison, present results to their engineering teams

  • Develop deep technical understanding of customer systems (retrieval pipelines, agentic workflows, code intelligence stacks) and design optimised Callosum workflows

  • Integrate Callosum workflows into customer environments and support them through to stable production

  • Work with our research and platform teams to turn what you learn into general product capability

  • Build the team's shared methodology: evaluation harnesses, integration runbooks, and engagement standards

What You Bring

  • Exceptional technical depth, demonstrated through any of: production systems at scale, research that shipped, or an early/founding role where you owned the system end to end

  • Experience with LLM serving infrastructure, agent orchestration, or retrieval systems

  • Rigour in evaluation or benchmarking work

  • A bias for action, comfort with ambiguity and a strong sense of ownership

What Sets You Apart

  • Experience working directly with external engineering teams, whether as a forward deployed engineer, solutions architect, technical consultant, or comparable customer-facing role

  • Familiarity with novel accelerator platforms

  • Experience at an early-stage company or in a founding-engineer role

What We Offer

  • Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience

jobs.title: 2027 Software Internship
jobs.description:
For over four decades, Cirrus Logic has been propelled by the top engineers in mixed-signal processing. Our rockstar team thrives on solving complex challenges with innovative end-user solutions for the world's top consumer brands. Cirrus Logic is also known for its award-winning culture, which was built on a foundation of inclusion and fairness, meaningful community engagement, and delivering enjoyable employee experiences at every turn. But we couldn’t do it without our extraordinary workforce – and that’s where you come in. Join our team and help us continue to make Cirrus Logic an exceptional place to grow your career! 

Cirrus Logic is looking for talented Summer and MEng Engineering Interns to join their experienced engineering teams in Edinburgh, Newbury and London, and work on industrial projects relevant to their degree.

This exciting opportunity includes openings in the following areas:

  • Embedded Firmware 
  • Software Tools 
  • Software Drivers 
  • System Test 

Summer placements are running between June and September.

MEng placements running between April and January.


Departmental Summary:
  • Embedded Firmware - You should be comfortable writing code in C/C++ and familiar with interpreted languages such as Python. With a strong background in signal processing, mathematical modelling, or algorithm design, you will collaborate with hardware designers to develop, debug, and optimize firmware, enabling the integration of innovative solutions onto commercial product platforms.
  • Software Tools - You will work alongside experienced software, hardware and UX engineers to create cross-platform desktop tools and developer workflows using technologies such as Java and Python. Your work could contribute to interactive configuration and tuning tools, automation, plugins or APIs used by engineering teams across the company. Experience with Java, Python, C++, C# or desktop application development is helpful, but not a must.
  • Software Drivers - You should be comfortable writing code in C and familiar with Linux kernel development, debugging tools, and automated test frameworks. With a strong background in computer science, electrical, electronic, or software engineering, and an interest in operating systems and embedded hardware, you will develop, debug, and optimize Linux (and MCU) device drivers, build and run automated tests through CI systems such as Jenkins, and work closely with cross-functional teams to enable reliable integration of commercial and consumer product platforms.
  • System Test - You should be comfortable writing code in Python and familiar with object-oriented languages like C++. With a background in electrical, electronic, computer, or software engineering and an interest in embedded systems and hardware/software integration, you will develop and run automated functional, system, and stress tests on real hardware, from FPGA emulation through to silicon.

    • Skills and Requirements:
  • Enrolled in MEng or BEng in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electronics and Electrical Engineering or a related subject degree and on track for a 2:1 or better
  • Some experience with development/evaluation of signal processing
  • Good understanding of software development principles
  • Interest in Embedded Systems
  • Excellent problem-solving ability
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

    • What to expect from your internship with Cirrus Logic:
  • Working on a detailed technical project relevant to your degree
  • Mentoring, coaching and development by top engineers
  • Interaction with other students and future leaders
  • Learning about our values and goals and experiencing a culture that fosters innovation, creativity, and timely execution
  • Develop your teamwork, planning, creative thinking, and problem-solving skills
  • A modern, state-of-the-art office environment in Edinburgh or Newbury
  • Competitive salary, great benefits, discounted lunches, on-site gymnasium, games area, jam room, happy hours, social events and free snacks, drinks & fruit
    • Candidates for this role must meet U.S. export control eligibility requirements. Due to U.S. export control restrictions and the short duration of this internship, we are unable to sponsor or obtain deemed export licenses for this role.
     
    Cirrus Logic follows a 2+ day in-office work schedule but interns should expect to be in the office more often, up to 5 days per week, based on business needs and team preference. Interns must be based within commutable distance of the work location listed on the job posting, or willing to relocate prior to beginning their internship with Cirrus Logic.

jobs.title: Oracle Fusion Solution Architect
Global Brand Relations Director
Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
About AQEMIA

AQEMIA is a drug invention company dedicated to creating entirely new medicines to address major unmet medical needs. At the core of our mission is QEMI, our proprietary molecule-invention platform, which uniquely combines cutting-edge science with advanced technology. Powered by physics-based modeling, statistical mechanics, and generative AI, QEMI allows our teams to design novel drug candidates from first principles.
 
What makes AQEMIA different is our commitment to true innovation: our research is dedicated to the invention of new molecular entities, not the refinement of existing ones. We focus on inventing never-before-seen molecules, without relying on experimental data, and advancing them into a growing pipeline of proprietary programs and strategic partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies.
 
Our most advanced preclinical programs are currently in vivo optimization, targeting diseases still waiting for effective treatments, offering our teams the opportunity to work on science that can make a real difference in people’s lives.
 
For more information, visit AQEMIA.com, our WTTJ Page, and our LinkedIn. 
 

About our Team

AQEMIA brings together a diverse, multidisciplinary team of 80+ professionals based in Paris and London. Our scientists and engineers, including chemists, physicists, machine learning experts, and software engineers, work side by side to push the boundaries of early-stage drug discovery.
 
This close collaboration across disciplines is central to our approach, enabling us to tackle complex scientific challenges from first principles and translate cutting-edge ideas into novel therapeutic candidates. At AQEMIA, team members are encouraged to contribute their expertise, learn from one another, and play an active role in shaping the future of drug invention.
 

About our Engineering Department

The Engineering team (~12 people) builds and scales the technical foundations that power Aqemia’s drug discovery engine.
 
Bringing together expertise across software engineering, cloud infrastructure, data engineering, site reliability engineering (SRE), and scientific computing, the team designs and operates robust, secure, and high-performance platforms that enable Aqemia’s scientific and AI teams to experiment, train, deploy, and run models at scale.
 
Their work spans data infrastructure, scientific compute systems, cloud operations, orchestration, observability, CI/CD, developer tooling, and platform scalability. By transforming cutting-edge research into reliable and scalable systems, the team accelerates the discovery of new medicines while ensuring operational excellence and an outstanding developer experience.

As Engineering Manager of the Compute team, you will lead a team of 5 engineers responsible for building and evolving the compute platform that powers AQEMIA's scientific simulations, machine learning workloads, and large-scale experimentation. You will combine strong engineering leadership with technical credibility to grow a high-performing team while delivering reliable and scalable platform capabilities.

Responsibilities

Lead and grow the Compute Engineering team

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of Software Engineers through regular feedback, career development and mentoring.

  • Foster a collaborative, inclusive and high-performing engineering culture built on ownership, trust and continuous improvement.

  • Recruit, onboard and retain exceptional engineering talent.

  • Help engineers grow both technically and professionally while creating clear development paths.

    • Deliver Compute roadmap

  • Partner with Product, Staff Engineers and Engineering Leadership to define priorities and execute the Compute roadmap.

  • Drive predictable delivery by supporting scientific computing, AI workloads and internal developer platforms.

  • Balance new capabilities, operational excellence and technical debt reduction.

  • Identify and proactively manage delivery risks, dependencies and execution challenges.

    • Ensure operational excellence

  • Drive high engineering standards across architecture, testing, observability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Improve the scalability, resilience and performance of production systems supporting research and platform teams.

  • Promote modern engineering practices including automation, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code and AI-assisted software development.

  • Continuously improve engineering processes, team effectiveness and operational maturity.

    • Partner across Engineering and Science

  • Collaborate closely with Platform, Data, AI and Scientific teams to translate research needs into scalable engineering solutions.

  • Facilitate communication between technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Ensure engineering execution remains aligned with AQEMIA's scientific objectives and business priorities.

  • Support cross-functional planning, architecture discussions and technical decision-making.

    • Contribute to Engineering leadership

  • Partner with Engineering Leadership on organizational planning, hiring strategy and team evolution.

  • Help define engineering standards, operating principles and best practices across the organization.

  • Contribute to long-term platform strategy and engineering scalability.

  • Foster knowledge sharing, technical excellence and continuous learning across teams.


    • Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in Software Engineering, including experience building production systems at scale.

  • Previous experience leading engineering teams as an Engineering Manager or Tech Lead with people management responsibilities.

  • Strong experience delivering distributed systems, cloud-native applications or compute-intensive platforms.

  • Solid software engineering background with hands-on experience in Python and modern backend development.

  • Experience working with AWS, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Snowflake and modern cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong understanding of software architecture, scalability, observability and operational excellence.

  • Experience leading roadmap execution and coordinating cross-functional engineering initiatives.

  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to influence across engineering, scientific and business stakeholders.

  • Strong coaching mindset with a passion for developing engineers and building high-performing teams.

  • Pragmatic approach to balancing delivery, technical excellence and organizational priorities.


    • Nice-to-have

  • Experience leading Platform Engineering, Infrastructure, Compute or SRE teams.

  • Exposure to scientific computing, machine learning infrastructure or AI platforms.

  • Familiarity with large-scale compute environments, GPU infrastructure or distributed training systems.

  • Experience with workflow orchestration systems and developer platforms.

  • Experience implementing AI-assisted engineering workflows and spec-driven development practices.

  • Track record of scaling engineering organizations in fast-growing technology companies.

  • Interest in computational chemistry, life sciences or scientific research environments.


    • Our Recruitment Process

    1. Talent Acquisition Interview (30 min) 

    2. Role Alignment & Leadership Interview with Hiring Manager (45 min) 

    3. Technical Assessment with a member of Engineering team (60 min) 

    4. Candidate Presentation + Q&A / Coffee (90 min)

    5. Culture Fit Interview with Emmanuelle, Co-founder & COO (60 min) 

    6. Final interview with Maximilien, Co-founder and CEO (60 min) 

    Why Join Us? 

    At AQEMIA, we work for a mission: joining us means having your own impact on changing the way drugs are discovered, and helping to shape the direction of our fast-growing company and team.
    Expanding Drug Discovery Pipeline : Focused on critical therapeutic areas like Oncology, CNS, Immuno-inflammation... with in vivo proof of concept/patent stage programs. Collaborations with top Pharma, including a $140M Sanofi deal.
    World-Class Interdisciplinary Team : work alongside exceptional talent at the intersection of technology and life sciences. Our teams combine deep expertise in AI, physics-based modeling, biology, and medicinal chemistry to push the boundaries of innovation.
    DeepTech Recognition: AQEMIA is proud to be part of the French Tech 40 and France 2030, highlighting our role as a key player in Europe’s DeepTech ecosystem.
    Prime Location with Flexibility : Our offices are located in the heart of Paris and London (King’s Cross), with flexible work arrangements including up to two remote days per week.
    Strong Financial Backing : $100M raised from leading European and International investors

jobs.title: GenAI Engineer (F/H/NB)
jobs.description:
SFEIR est un cabinet d'expertise technologique spécialisé dans la conception, l'architecture et l'industrialisation de solutions numériques sur-mesure. Nous accompagnons les organisations dans leurs transformations les plus complexes en combinant la rigueur du Software Craftsmanship avec la maîtrise des technologies d'avenir. Convaincus que la souveraineté numérique est un enjeu stratégique majeur, nous concevons des architectures sécurisées, performantes et indépendantes, portées par des partenariats solides avec des acteurs clés comme SENS et Scaleway. Acteur de référence sur l'intelligence artificielle, nous faisons évoluer les standards d'ingénierie modernes. À travers notre plateforme GenAI RAISE et notre statut de partenaire Anthropic Select (au sein du Claude Partner Network), nous plaçons le Context Engineering et l'IA générative au cœur de nos pratiques. 

Nos chiffres clés :

  • 950 consultants passionnés par la tech et augmentés par l’IA.
  • 8 agences en France, au Luxembourg et en Belgique.
  • Partenaire Anthropic Select au sein du Claude Partner Network.
  • 15 ans de partenariat avec Google Cloud, AWS, Microsoft, Databricks, Confluent...
  • +5000 personnes formées par an via le SFEIR Institute.

Rejoindre SFEIR, c'est intégrer un collectif où la culture technique prévaut. Nous offrons des trajectoires de carrière dédiées aux experts (Individual Contributor / IC), te permettant de progresser en haute maîtrise technique sans devoir basculer vers du management organisationnel. Nous intégrons l'IA à nos propres pratiques d'ingénierie (utilisation quotidienne de RAISE et Claude Code) pour automatiser les tâches à faible valeur ajoutée et concentrer nos efforts sur la conception d'architectures résilientes.

▪️ À propos de la mission

En tant qu'Expert & Trainer GenAI, tu t'inscris à la croisée de l'ingénierie logicielle, de la formation d'élite et du conseil stratégique. Tu es le garant de la mise en œuvre pragmatique et sécurisée de l'IA chez nos clients.

Architecture & Ingénierie GenAI

Tu concois, pilotes et déploies des architectures GenAI robustes et prêtes pour la production :

  • Model Engineering & Contexte : Arbitrage et choix des LLMs (Claude, Gemini, GPT, Open Source), optimisation des paramètres (fenêtre de contexte, context caching, system prompts) et maîtrise du Model Context Protocol (MCP).

  • Pipelines Avancés & RAG : Conception de stratégies de retrieval complexes (chunking, bases vectorielles, GraphRAG, hybride) et orchestration de workflows agentiques (LangChain, LangGraph, Google ADK, patterns ReAct).

  • Industrialisation & FinOps : Évaluation de la fiabilité (LLM-as-a-judge), maîtrise des coûts au token, guardrails de sécurité (AI Act, prompt injection, étanchéité des données) et déploiement multi-cloud (Vertex AI, Bedrock, Azure OpenAI).

Formation & Transmission "Développeur Augmenté" (SFEIR Institute)

Tu es le visage de l'excellence pédagogique de SFEIR. Tu conçois et animes nos parcours phares (jusqu'à 60% de pratique / labs) pour transformer les méthodes de dev chez nos clients :

  • Agentic Coding : Acculturation aux workflows de développement assisté (Specify → Plan → Tasks → Implement → Validate) via des outils comme Claude Code, GitHub Copilot ou Gemini CLI.

  • Standardisation d'équipe : Diffusion des bonnes pratiques de gestion de contexte (CLAUDE.md, règles modulaires, génération de tests) et création de serveurs MCP sécurisés.

  • Pédagogie & Regard Critique : Vulgarisation adaptative (du décideur à l'ingénieur) tout en insufflant une culture de la sécurité (code review, vulnérabilités) et du maintien des compétences en dev classique.

Conseil & Stratégie GenAI

Tu transformes des besoins métiers complexes ou flous en feuilles de route opérationnelles et à fort ROI :

  • Cadrage & Roadmap : Animation d'ateliers d'idéation, priorisation des cas d'usage (Quick Wins vs Chantiers structurants) et construction du business case pour les sponsors.

  • Architecture de Solutions : Arbitrages Build vs Buy, conception de couches intermédiaires (Context Graphs) pour maîtriser la dette technique et l'économie du token.

  • Gouvernance & Change : Accompagnement des instances dirigeantes (COMEX, CODIR) sur la gestion du risque, la conformité et la conduite du changement.

▪️ Le profil idéal

Formation & Parcours : Titulaire d'un Bac+5 en informatique (école d'ingénieur ou Master universitaire) ou bénéficiant d'une solide expérience terrain équivalente dans la conception logicielle et l'architecture système.

Expérience : Tu justifies d'au moins 5 ans d'expérience globale en ingénierie logicielle ou architecture cloud, avec une spécialisation marquée et récente en IA générative, ingénierie de prompt et orchestration agentique. Une première expérience réussie en formation/consulting ou une appétence forte pour la transmission est indispensable.

▪️ L'ancrage Bordelais

L'agence SFEIR Bordeaux regroupe une quinzaine d'ingénieurs et d'architectes seniors. Tu y trouveras la proximité et l'agilité d'une structure à taille humaine, adossée à la solidité d'un grand groupe. Tu participes activement à l'écosystème tech local (meetups, conférences BDX/IO, SFEIR Talks) et tu peux intégrer le programme AI Champions pour piloter la R&D de l'agence.

▪️ Tes conditions de travail 

  • Organisation : 2 à 3 jours de télétravail par semaine.
  • Équipement : Laptop haut de gamme au choix (MacBook Pro ou Dell Precision dernière génération).
  • Package : Rémunération fixe attractive, prime de vacances, accord d'intéressement, forfait mobilités durables, mutuelle et titres-restaurant.

▪️ Le processus de recrutement 

  1. Échange RH : Alignement sur ton parcours, tes attentes et les opportunités SFEIR.
  2. Session Technique ("PlayOffs") : Évaluation pratique en pair-programming (Algo, Python, GenAI) avec trois Sfeirians.
  3. Échange Métier & Projection : Discussion approfondie sur les cas d'usage, les missions cibles et le contexte client à Bordeaux.
  4. Entretien Final : Échange stratégique avec le Directeur d'Agence.

About Voodoo

jobs.description:
ENGLISH VERSION

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !

Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.

Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.

🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vous

Ce post-doctorat s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet ANR PRME LINEN (Experimental and Numerical Characterisation of Flax Composite Manufacturing by Liquid Infusion: From Local Phenomena to Induced Properties), auquel participent plusieurs chercheurs de l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne, avec pour objectif d’étudier l’élaboration de pièces structurales en matériaux composites à base de fibres de lin.

Ce post-doctorat, d’une durée de 12 mois est proposé pour développer la modélisation numérique de l’infusion de résine dans des préformes composites à fibres de lin. L’objectif est d’étudier, à l’échelle mésoscopique, l’influence de l’organisation anisotrope et hétérogène des torons de fibres sur l’écoulement de la résine. Le projet s’appuiera sur des simulations 3D par éléments finis, reposant sur un couplage Stokes-Darcy et la prise en compte d’un tenseur de perméabilité orthotrope. Une attention particulière sera portée à l’influence des variations locales de la fraction volumique de fibres sur la perméabilité, les chemins préférentiels d’écoulement et les effets capillaires. Les simulations seront réalisées avec le code éléments finis Cœur (https://gitlab.emse.fr/bruchon/Coeur), en s’appuyant sur la bibliothèque PETSc et des solveurs itératifs préconditionnés adaptés aux problèmes de grande taille. Dans un premier temps, des architectures idéalisées de type unidirectionnel, quasi-unidirectionnel et tissé seront étudiées à l’aide d’une représentation par Level-Set. Dans un second temps, lorsque cela sera possible, des mésostructures réalistes seront reconstruites à partir d’images µ-CT.

Le post-doctorant.e contribuera également au développement et à la validation de la stratégie numérique et travaillera en interaction étroite avec les travaux expérimentaux et numériques des autres tâches du projet.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Une formation en mécanique numérique, mécanique des fluides, éléments finis ou calcul scientifique est recherchée.

Des compétences en C++/Python, calcul haute performance, PETSc, méthodes Level-Set ou traitement d’images 3D seront appréciées.

Vous vous reconnaissez dans les capacités et aptitudes suivantes :

· Capacité à travailler en équipe

· Capacité à dialoguer avec des interlocuteurs académiques et industriels

Les candidats retenus après examen de leur dossier de candidature seront auditionnés en entretien par visioconférence puis, le cas échéant, reçus pour un entretien en présentiel à Mines Saint-Étienne.

Dans le cadre de sa politique Égalité, Diversité et Inclusion, l’École des Mines de Saint Etienne est un employeur soucieux de l’équité de traitement entre les candidatures.
